questions.question: Dr Chafik has been running his practice in commercial premises for 3 years. According to Article 4 of Law 49-16, what fundamental right does he automatically acquire?
options: The right to sublet without any conditions
The right to renewal of the lease
The right to change the use of the premises
The right to assign his lease without informing the landlord
questions.explanation: Art. 4: the tenant benefits from the right to renewal of the lease when he proves continuous enjoyment for at least two years.

questions.question: Dr Malak paid a 'key money' of 150,000 DH when signing his lease. According to Article 4, what advantage does this give him?
options: An automatic reduction of his monthly rent
An exemption from the two-year duration requirement for renewal
A right of pre-emption on the neighboring premises
A total exemption from rental charges
questions.explanation: Art. 4, para. 2: the tenant is exempt from the duration condition if he has paid a sum of money in consideration for the right to the lease.

questions.question: Dr Chafik notices that his landlord is asking for charges not provided for in the lease. According to Article 5, what should he do?
options: Accept without question because the landlord is always right
Contest because charges are considered included in the rent if not stipulated
Pay immediately under penalty of eviction
Seize the court before any payment
questions.explanation: Art. 5, para. 2: in the absence of a stipulation as to which party bears the charges, they are considered to be included in the rent.

questions.question: Dr Malak wishes to contest a rent revision he considers excessive. According to Article 5, which law governs this revision?
options: Law No. 65-00 relating to health insurance
Law No. 07-03 relating to the revision of the amount of rent
Law No. 9-88 relating to accounting obligations
Law No. 15-95 forming the commercial code
questions.explanation: Art. 5, para. 3: the revision of the rent is subject to the provisions of Law No. 07-03.

questions.question: Dr Chafik's lease contains a clause stating that he waives his right to renewal. According to Article 6, what is the validity of this clause?
options: It is valid because freely consented to
It is null and void because any stipulation contrary to the law is null
It is valid for the first 3 years only
It is subject to court approval
questions.explanation: Art. 6: leases governed by the law only terminate by application of Article 26. Any contrary stipulation is null.

questions.question: Dr Malak's landlord wishes to evict him. According to Article 7, must the eviction compensation be paid?
options: No, compensation is optional
Yes, except in the cases of exemption provided for in Article 8
No, it is only due if the tenant requests it
Yes, automatically without any exception
questions.explanation: Art. 7 and 8: the tenant is entitled to compensation subject to the exceptions provided for by law (Article 8).

questions.question: According to Article 7, on what basis is the value of the business calculated for Dr Chafik's eviction compensation?
options: On the value estimated by the landlord
On the tax declarations of the last four financial years
On the turnover of the last month
On the purchase value of the dental equipment
questions.explanation: Art. 7, para. 3: the compensation includes the value of the business estimated on the basis of the tax declarations for the last four financial years.

questions.question: Dr Malak has not paid his rent for 4 months. According to Article 8, can the landlord evict him without compensation?
options: Yes, after formal notice remaining unsuccessful for 15 days
No, compensation is always due
Yes, only if the delay exceeds 6 months
No, the landlord must first seize the court
questions.explanation: Art. 8, 1°: the landlord is not liable for compensation when the tenant has not paid within 15 days after formal notice for an amount equivalent to at least 3 months.

questions.question: Dr Chafik has transformed his practice without his landlord's consent. According to Article 8, what does he risk?
options: Eviction without compensation, unless he restores the premises within 3 months
A simple flat-rate fine
An automatic rent increase
No sanction because transformations are free
questions.explanation: Art. 8, 2°: the landlord is exempt from compensation if the tenant transforms the premises, unless he restores the premises within a period not exceeding 3 months.

questions.question: Dr Malak's landlord wants to demolish and rebuild the building. According to Article 9, what is the prerequisite for eviction?
options: Obtain the tenant's consent
Prove ownership for one year from the date of the notice
Pay a deposit of 1,000,000 DH
Obtain the agreement of all co-owners
questions.explanation: Art. 9, para. 1: the landlord must prove ownership for a period of at least one year from the date of the notice.

questions.question: In the event of demolition-reconstruction, what provisional compensation must Dr Chafik receive according to Article 9?
options: The equivalent of 6 months' rent
The equivalent of 3 years' rent
The equivalent of 5 years' rent
The equivalent of 1 year's rent
questions.explanation: Art. 9, para. 1: the landlord must pay a provisional compensation equivalent to three years' rent.

questions.question: According to Article 9, if the new building does not contain similar premises, what right does Dr Malak retain?
options: He loses all right to compensation
He is entitled to full compensation in accordance with Article 7
He must accept any premises offered
He can demand the construction of custom premises
questions.explanation: Art. 9, para. 4: when the new building does not contain the said premises, the tenant shall be entitled to compensation in accordance with the provisions of Article 7.

questions.question: Dr Chafik's landlord evicted him for demolition. According to Article 10, within what time limit must he start the works?
options: Within 1 month
Within 2 months
Within 3 months
Within 6 months
questions.explanation: Art. 10: the landlord is required to start the reconstruction within two months from the date of eviction.

questions.question: According to Article 11, what is the maximum time limit for making the new premises available to Dr Malak after demolition?
options: 1 year
2 years
3 years
5 years
questions.explanation: Art. 11, para. 1: the premises must be handed over within a period not exceeding three years from the date of eviction.

questions.question: Dr Chafik's landlord wishes to raise the building. According to Article 16, what is the maximum duration of temporary eviction?
options: 6 months
1 year
2 years
3 years
questions.explanation: Art. 16, para. 1: the duration of temporary eviction cannot exceed one year from the date of eviction.

questions.question: According to Article 16, what compensation does Dr Malak receive during the temporary eviction period?
options: The amount of profits based on the tax declarations of the previous financial year
A flat-rate amount of 50,000 DH
The equivalent of 6 months' rent
Only reimbursement of moving costs
questions.explanation: Art. 16, para. 2: the compensation corresponds to the loss suffered, not exceeding the amount of profits based on the tax declarations of the previous financial year.

questions.question: According to Article 18, what document must the landlord absolutely produce for an eviction for demolition?
options: A simple registered letter
A valid building permit and an approved plan
A certificate from the town hall
An agreement from the neighbors
questions.explanation: Art. 18, para. 1: the landlord must produce a valid building permit and a plan approved by the competent authority.

questions.question: Dr Chafik wishes to sublet part of his practice. According to Article 24, what is the applicable rule?
options: Subletting is always prohibited
Subletting is authorized unless otherwise stipulated in the lease
Subletting is only authorized with the written consent of the landlord
Subletting is only authorized to a colleague
questions.explanation: Art. 24, para. 1: the tenant may sublet all or part of the premises, unless otherwise stipulated.

questions.question: According to Article 24, if the sublease rent exceeds the main rent, can Dr Malak's landlord take action?
options: No, he has no right to the sublease rent
Yes, he is entitled to a revision of the rent amicably or by judicial means
Yes, but only if the difference exceeds 50%
No, subletting is completely free
questions.explanation: Art. 24, last para.: when the value of the sublease exceeds that of the main lease, the lessor is entitled to a revision of the rent amicably or by judicial means.

questions.question: Dr Chafik wishes to assign his lease. According to Article 25, does he need the landlord's consent?
options: Yes, the written consent of the landlord is mandatory
No, he can do it without consent and notwithstanding any contrary stipulation
Yes, but only if he assigns with the business
No, but he must inform the landlord within 15 days
questions.explanation: Art. 25, para. 1: the tenant has the right to assign the lease without the lessor's agreement and notwithstanding any contrary stipulation.

questions.question: According to Article 25, from when is Dr Malak's lease assignment enforceable against the landlord?
options: From the signing of the assignment deed
From the date of notification to the landlord
From the publication in the commercial register
From acceptance by the landlord
questions.explanation: Art. 25, para. 3: the assignment is only enforceable against the lessor from the date of notification.

questions.question: According to Article 26, what is the eviction period for a serious reason such as non-compliance with the lease clauses?
options: 15 days
1 month
3 months
6 months
questions.explanation: Art. 26, para. 2: the period is set at 3 months when the request is based on a serious reason relating to the tenant's non-compliance with the lease clauses.

questions.question: According to Article 26, within what time limit is Dr Chafik's landlord forfeited from the right to request validation of the notice?
options: After 3 months from the expiry of the period granted to the tenant
After 6 months from the expiry of the period granted to the tenant
After 1 year from the expiry of the period granted to the tenant
After 2 years from the expiry of the period granted to the tenant
questions.explanation: Art. 26, para. 6: the lessor is forfeited from the right to request validation of the notice after six months from the expiry of the period granted to the tenant.

questions.question: According to Article 27, can Dr Malak request compensation during the action for validation of the notice?
options: No, he must wait for the final judgment
Yes, he may file a request for compensation
Yes, but only after eviction
No, compensation is fixed only by the landlord
questions.explanation: Art. 27, para. 2: the tenant may file a request for compensation during the action for validation of the notice.

questions.question: According to Article 28, within what time limit must the landlord deposit the amount of compensation after an eviction judgment?
options: Within 1 month
Within 2 months
Within 3 months
Within 6 months
questions.explanation: Art. 28: the lessor is required to deposit the amount of compensation within a period of three months from the date on which the judgment becomes enforceable.

questions.question: According to Article 33, if Dr Chafik's lease contains a resolutory clause, after how many months of unpaid rent can the landlord take action?
options: After 1 month of arrears
After 2 months of arrears
After 3 months of arrears
After 6 months of arrears
questions.explanation: Art. 33: the lessor may take action in default of payment of rent by the tenant for a period of three months, after formal notice remaining unsuccessful for 15 days.
